descriptionChirho: To have a desire or inclination for something; the basic volitional sense expressing a subject's want or desire, across all persons, tenses, and moods (Arabic أَرَادَ/يُرِيدُ, Korean 원하다, Swahili -taka).

To have something in mind as a purpose or intention; the purposive/volitional sense expressing resolve or divine determination, often in contexts where God or an authority figure 'wills' an outcome (Arabic شَاءَ, English 'wills', 'he willed').

To be disposed or ready to do something; emphasizes willingness or readiness rather than active desire, often appearing where the subject agrees or consents to act (English 'be willing', 'was willing', Arabic أَرَادَ in concessive contexts).
To wish for something, often with an optative or counterfactual nuance; expresses longing or a wish that may not be realized (Spanish 'deseaba/quisiera', Swahili -penda, Arabic كُنتُ أُريدُ).

To take pleasure or delight in something; the affective sense where θέλω expresses enjoyment or preference rather than mere volition (English 'delighting', 'desires'; Arabic الرّاغِبُ; Swahili -penda in affective contexts).
